title: Siman

paragraphs: [Bava Batra 113a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.113a.3-5) has “Siman: Rabbah bar Rav Shila said.” Masoret HaShas suggests Siman may be a sage’s name.[^1]

Hyman considers it more likely that a mnemonic label is missing: אימ״ם, from the scriptural words ish, yidbakenu, matot and mimateh. Alternatively, he proposes the mnemonic בחב״ש, formed from the names of the Amoraim offering answers there. He cites the author of Dikdukei Soferim, note 9, for this view.[^2]

notes.text: The word siman precedes Rabbah bar Rav Shila’s proposal. It can mean a mnemonic, and Hyman offers two ways to account for it.
The linked text gives successive interpretations of the scriptural wording. The readings ascribed to Masoret HaShas and Dikdukei Soferim are Hyman’s reports.
